chapter: New York scene and bebop community
title: First recordings with Foots Thomas and his Savoy date
summary: His first records were with Walter Foots Thomas alongside veterans, then his first date under his own name for Savoy.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You mentioned earlier the recording of the Mad Monk. Was this your first recording?
Yes, that was the recording date that I did for Savoy Records.
This is your first recording and it’s under your name?
It was my first recording under my name. I had actually recorded with Foots Thomas and some other people on records with them.
Do you remember anything that’s memorable about that first recording experience or perhaps the one that you did under your name?

In the earlier records with Foots Thomas I was always awed by the fact that the musicians that he chose were the musicians that I had seen work with the big bands. They came from Cab Calloway’s band, Fletcher Henderson’s band and so forth, and these were guys who I had always looked up to as guys that I would like to emulate, to be like these guys, and here I am on my first series of record dates with them… and

Emmett Barry and Bill Coleman and guys like that who were just wonderful players. So it was very exciting. Coleman Hawkins and Charlie Shavers, you know, you’ve got all these very, very fine musicians who have much to say and who were very helpful, didn’t let me get nervous and just relaxed me and helped me get through the job.
